_productModel: LegalEase asks the participant structured questions, relies on their answers, generates the applicable packet, names the documents they may need to obtain and attach, and gives filing instructions. It does not require, accept, inspect or authenticate third-party records; it does not determine eligibility; it does not approve a filing; it does not guarantee court action. So participantInputs are questions, supportingDocuments are things the participant goes and gets, and neither the certified disposition below nor any other record delays generation.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Non-Conviction Records
tracks.publicName: Clear a case that did not end in conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: Example: on petition the court shall expunge records of an arrest that ended in dismissal, acquittal or no disposition.

exclusions: Example: cases with an outstanding warrant.

geography.venue: The trial court where the case was filed.

destination.name: Clerk of the trial court
destination.detail: File in the county where the charge originated. Serve the prosecutor.

components.notes: No official form; generated from an approved template.

components.conditionDescription: Applies only when the petitioner requests a fee waiver.

tracks._participantInputsNote: What LegalEase asks. These are the participant's answers, and generation runs on them. Note that the disposition is asked as a question here, while the certified disposition itself is a supporting document below.

participantInputs.question: In which county were you arrested or charged?
How did the case end — dismissed, acquitted, charges dropped, or no disposition?
On what date did the case end?
Was the dismissal with prejudice or without?
participantInputs.conditionDescription: Asked only when the disposition is a dismissal, because it sets the waiting period.

tracks._supportingDocumentsNote: What the participant obtains and attaches. LegalEase lists these in the packet instructions. It does not require them before generating, does not take uploads of them, and does not inspect or authenticate them.

supportingDocuments.name: Certified disposition for each charge
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the trial court where the case was filed
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Example: ask the clerk's office for a certified copy of the disposition. Most counties charge a per-copy fee.

supportingDocuments.name: State criminal-history record
supportingDocuments.conditionDescription: Only when the court asks for one at the hearing.
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Example: request a personal review copy from the state bureau.

tracks._manualCompletionNote: What the generated packet deliberately leaves blank.

manualCompletionItems.why: The court requires the petitioner's own wet signature.
The clerk assigns the date when the petition is filed.

rules.filing: File the petition and proposed order with the clerk of the trial court.
rules.notice: Example: the prosecutor receives notice and has 30 days to object.
rules.service: Example: serve the prosecutor by mail; file proof of service.
rules.participantSignature: Example: the petitioner signs the petition. A wet signature is required.

selfHelpStopConditions: The court sets a contested hearing.
The petitioner has an open case or outstanding warrant.
